title: Congo Square pictured and the Zolipon dance
summary: Russell shows an old Congo Square picture; she says there were only trees and recalls the Zolipon dance there.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, last fall, you were telling us about those dances when that man from New York, Marshall Stearns, was here. And you mentioned you'd seen some dances in the old Congo Square. What kind of dances did they have there? On the Congo Square?
Danse Creole. Creole dance. Can you see this picture? Is there enough light here?

This is an old picture that we found that says Congo Square. I can't tell which direction that's looking or anything. Do you have enough light on that to see it? Turn the light on there. They have a lot of trees there.
And there's some building.

That's where the auditorium is now. But I don't know which way of the living. It's not the auditorium. Did it look like that? Do you know any time when it looked about like that, those trees? Those trees, yes. But this I don't remember.
But this, I don't remember that.
That building, you don't remember?
No. That, yes.
Did they have anything in the square in those days at all?
They had what?
What did they have in the square? Did they have any buildings?
No, no. They didn't have nothing in the square. Nothing but the trees. And there where they would go, there where they would go and dance, Creole dance.
What? Do you remember what they sang when they danced? Was there a song about when the potato is cooked, we will eat it? Con la patate, something, nous mangeons, comme ça.
Did you just give me a glass? No, I got my window glass.
I don't remember. Mais tout nard, les yers, oui.
Did you do a whiskey? Or when I give you a bottle of coke, you get another bottle. Another glass there. I don't know. Yeah.
They used to dance, Zolipon, on the square.
Zolipon?
Zolipon.
What is that?

That's a dance. They dance, they hold a dress. Zolipon, Zolipon Mambo. Zolipon, gardez comme l'icard. Zolipon, ah, Zolipon Mambo. And then they put a bottle and they put over it like that. They say, Sayamaku Pesa. Sayamaku Pesa. That was some African song, I suppose. By damn trees. Well, let's give you to Mr. Russell.

That's an old picture we got from Raymond Burke that he found someplace. That's Congo Square. I don't know what that building is. In your mother's time, she said there was no building there. That might be on the edge of the square, too. It might be even on that street.
Yes, it is, because Congo Square was the... Congo Square didn't have no house around.
Do you remember when there was an old parish prison back up there, too? Yes. Before my time. Yeah. You don't remember that?
